1	# Toolbar control-layer design — synthesis (panel of 3 + grounding)
2	
3	Inputs: `design-model-first.md`, `design-ownership-first.md`, `design-consumer-first.md` (each designed from the brief, no code), plus one grounding read of `use-job-output.ts`.
4	
5	## 1. Strong consensus — the spine (all three, independently). High confidence.
6	
7	1. **Drop `filters`/`actions`.** The taxonomy axis is **effect on the data pipeline**, not UI affordance: does the control's state (a) cross the network, (b) re-project loaded rows client-side, (c) fire a stateless command, or (d) is it a read-only derived display.
8	2. **A flat descriptor registry IS the interface.** Each control is a self-describing `ControlDescriptor` (id, category, value, onChange, isActive, clear, label, describe→chip, focus, syncKey). The toolbar takes ~3 props (registry + imperative actions + derived/meta). Adding a control never changes the toolbar's signature.
9	3. **The chip row is 100% derived** — a projection over the registry: `registry.filter(chipable && isActive && describe(value)!=null)`. No hand-maintained chip list; chip→control focus is structurally always wired (the chip is a view of its descriptor).
10	4. **Per-key opt-in URL sync** (`syncKey`/`urlSync` on each descriptor; a useQSync-style dict over only the opted-in keys). Default = not synced, so "sync everything" is structurally impossible. Sync rule: low-cardinality AND job-portable AND shareable. Column-keyed maps (hidden-cols, column-scope, reorder) NEVER sync.
11	5. **A new `useOutputViewState` hook** owns all client-only state; `useJobOutput` keeps the fetch-affecting settings; the two are **siblings that never call each other**; a thin **composer** (`useToolbarInterface`, owns no state) reads both and assembles the registry. This is what keeps `useJobOutput` from becoming the dumping ground while the toolbar sees one unified interface.
12	6. **A reducer inside the view hook** — gives stable `dispatch` (→ stable mutator refs → memo is a free later add), makes bulk-apply (load saved view) one dispatch, and makes saved-views trivial (serialize one state object).
13	7. **Smart-defaults waterfall**: `metadata → default resolver → initial control state`, precedence **URL > saved-view > smart-default > hard fallback**, computed once per `jobId`. Defaults seed _initial_ state only; they don't re-drive.
14	8. **Saved filter views (deferred) = a serialized snapshot of the shaping subset.** Needs NO new concept — the model already names the exact subset a view captures. This is the test that proved the model right to all three.
15	9. **The two reusable primitives fall out for free**: "toolbar-option button + dropdown-card" (FAB/export/re-run share a shell) and "selection option list" (columns-to-search/hide are the same multi-select).
16	10. **Memo is additive, not a redesign** — if descriptors are reference-stable (mutators from dispatch, descriptor object memoized on its value, derivations as selectors), `React.memo` on each per-concern leaf just captures stability that already exists. Presentation state (search-expanded, panel-open) must live in the leaf, never the interface, or it re-renders the whole toolbar.
17	
18	## 2. Grounding correction (from `use-job-output.ts`)
19	
20	The query key = `GetJobOutput(jobId) + fab.mode + fab.delimiter + tabToShow` (`:73-76`).
21	
22	- **FETCH-SHAPE (crosses network):** `format/FAB`, `active sheet`. Owned by `useJobOutput`. ✅ as the panels assumed.
23	- **status filter is NOT fetch-affecting.** It filters `allRows` client-side (`:154-156`) and is absent from the query key. All three panels (and the brief) misclassified it as fetch-affecting. **In the real model status is VIEW-SHAPE** and is currently misfiled inside `useJobOutput` — in the redesign it moves to `useOutputViewState`. This shrinks the fetch-owned set to exactly two controls.
24	
25	## 3. Bridge to the existing code — this is an evolution, not a rewrite
26	
27	The current `appliedFilters` object in `preview-job-modal.title.tsx:112-182` is **already a proto-descriptor-registry**: each entry has `value / onChange / clear / active / getLabel / Icon / focusMode` — that is a `ControlDescriptor` minus `category`/`chipable`/`syncKey`. `appliedFilterState` (`:187`) is already the chip projection. So the recommended design = **lift `appliedFilters` into `useOutputViewState`, add the 3 missing fields, keep the chip projection**. The "memoize the fuck out of this" TODO (`:111`) is solved for free by moving it behind the reducer-backed hook (stable dispatch refs).
28	
29	## 4. The decisions that are genuinely OURS (where the panels diverged)
30	
31	| #   | Decision                                       | Options                                                                                                         | Lean                                                                                                                        |
32	| --- | ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
33	| D1  | Category granularity                           | 4 cats (fold display toggles into view) vs 5 (DISPLAY-PREF as its own)                                          | **Fold** — only fetch-vs-client + chipable actually drive behaviour; a 3rd "display" category buys nothing mechanical       |
34	| D2  | `isActive` baseline                            | compare to NEUTRAL (defaulted filters still chip — transparency) vs to SMART-DEFAULT (chip only on user change) | **Your call** — affects chip count on first open; scraper jobs with many defaulted hidden cols could be noisy under neutral |
35	| D3  | `activeSheet` sync                             | sync it (deep-link to a sheet) vs not; either way its sync crosses the hook boundary (it's fetch-owned)         | flag as a deliberate add; lean **don't sync v1**                                                                            |
36	| D4  | navigation modeling                            | a role-tag on a fetch-shape control (model-first) vs its own category (others)                                  | **role-tag** — sheet is the only nav control; a whole category for one is overkill                                          |
37	| D5  | ephemeral UI (search-expanded, FAB-panel-open) | leaf-local, never in the interface (model/consumer) vs a descriptor (ownership)                                 | **leaf-local** — keeping it out of the data interface is half of why filters/actions felt wrong                             |
38	
39	## 5. Verify before implementing
40	
41	- **`useJobOutput` return stability** — do `outputRows` / the setters keep identity across renders? The whole memo payoff assumes yes; if it returns fresh objects per render, a normalization layer comes first. (Cheap to check.)
42	- **Will column-scope / multi-sheet-search need the server?** If searching un-loaded sheets needs a fetch, parts of search become FETCH-SHAPE and move owners. (Currently search is pure client-side over `outputRows`.)
43	
44	## 6. Recommended sequence (when we implement — your hands)
45	
46	1. **Descriptor + registry + `chips()` selector**, built from the _existing_ `appliedFilters` controls (status, search, col-hide, format, expand, show-metadata). Prove chips derive with no hand-list and focus-on-click wires for free. Smallest, highest-confidence step.
47	2. **`useOutputViewState` reducer** — move status + search + col-scope + hidden-cols + toggles in; leave `format` + `sheet` in `useJobOutput`; wire the thin composer. This is the "reconcile the scattered state" step.
48	3. **Per-key URL sync** via the descriptor `syncKey` dict (status, search, toggles in; maps out).
49	4. **Memo pass LAST** — `React.memo` on each per-concern leaf once the refs are stable. Per your constraint: design first, memo once it makes sense without it.
50	5. (Deferred) saved-views = snapshot/restore the shaping subset; (separate task) RenderColumns break-up.

# Server Actions & Server Component Rules

These rules activate for files in `src/app/` and `src/data/`.

## Server Actions

When creating a Server Action:

1. **Always add `'use server'` directive** at the top of the file or function
2. **Validate input with Zod** — never trust client-supplied data
3. **Check auth** before performing any mutation:
   ```typescript
   const session = await getServerSession(authOptions);
   if (!session?.user) throw new Error("Unauthorized");
   ```
4. Return a typed result — use a discriminated union `{ success: true, data } | { success: false, error }` pattern

## Data Files (`*.data.ts`)

- `src/data/*.data.ts` files are Server Component data access functions — server-only
- These functions are called directly in page/layout Server Components, never in Client Components
- Always mark with `import "server-only"` or use `withServer` guard from `src/utils/with-server.ts`
- Do not call these from `route.ts` — they're for RSC only; use `src/db/` queries in API routes

## Server/Client Boundary

- **Server files:** `*.server.ts`, `*.data.ts` — can import from server-only packages
- **Client files:** `*.client.ts`, `'use client'` components — cannot import server-only modules
- If a file needs to work in both contexts, it must be isomorphic (no server-only imports)
- Use `withServer` from `src/utils/with-server.ts` to guard server-only modules

## TanStack Query Invalidation

After any mutation (Server Action or API route), invalidate the relevant TanStack Query keys on the client:

```typescript
// In the useM hook caller:
onSuccess: () => {
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: QueryKeys.resource(id) });
};
```

Failing to invalidate leaves stale data in TanStack Query's in-memory cache (retained for `gcTime`). Note: this app uses a plain `QueryClientProvider` in `app-wrapper.client.tsx` — there is **no** `PersistQueryClientProvider`, so the cache is not persisted to localStorage. Explicit invalidation is still required after every mutation.

Verified. Here's the stable-refs verdict and the spec, then I'll build it.

## Stable-refs verdict (static analysis — confirmed)

The load-bearing pieces in `useJobOutput` **are** reference-stable: TanStack's `structuralSharing` is on (not disabled anywhere) so `outputResponse` keeps its ref until the data actually changes; `outputRows/allRows/statusCounts/metadata` are `useMemo`'d on `[outputResponse, status, jobStatus]`; setters and `refetchOutput` are stable. The *only* non-stable bits are the return **wrapper objects** (`{data}`, `{options}`, …) — fresh literals each render. So memo works as long as consumers read the individual values, not the wrappers. **No normalization layer needed.**

One thing this surfaced: `useOptions`'s setters are recreated every render (not stable). That's why for the view hook I'm using `useReducer` (merge-patch) — its `dispatch` is stable, which is what makes the deferred memo a mechanical add. `useOptions` was the alternative (it's your existing primitive) but its fresh setters would fight the memo goal you set. If you'd rather stay on `useOptions`, say so and I'll switch.

## Spec for steps 1+2

**The view-state hook** (step 2) — one home for the scattered client state:
```
useOutputViewState() -> [view, setView]
  view: { search, columnsToSearch, hiddenColumns{per-sheet}, status, expandCells, showMetadataCols, showFabOptions }
  setView({ search: "x" })   // merge-patch, stable dispatch
```
`status` moves here from `useJobOutput` (it's client-side — confirmed). `useJobOutput` takes `itemStatusFilter` as an input instead of owning it (only the modal reads its status setter, so nothing else breaks; the validation caller doesn't touch status).

**The registry** (step 1) — one control per chip, no hand-kept list:
```
ToolbarControl = { id, active, chip, label, Icon, clear, focusMode? }
buildOutputControls({ view, setView, fabOptions, setFabOptions, activeSheet }) -> ToolbarControl[]
toChips(controls) = controls.filter(c => c.chip && c.active)
```
(No `value`/`onChange` yet — chips don't consume them, and the widgets still set state directly. Those join the descriptor when the widgets adopt the registry, with their callers — not before.)

**How it plugs into the UI:** the modal owns `useOutputViewState`, builds `controls`, and passes `chips={toChips(controls)}` to the title. The title's chip row renders from `chips` (deleting its `appliedFilters` + `appliedFilterState`). The widgets keep their current props, re-sourced from `view` through the modal — so the title change is just the chip row.

Building it now.

## What landed

```
useOutputViewState (merge-reducer) ─┐
   owns: search, columnsToSearch,    │
```
